questionText:
If $A = \{a, b\}$ and $B = \{10, 20\}$, then which of the following option(s) is/ are binary relation from $A$ to $B$?
I. $\{(a, 10), (b, 20)\}$
II. $\{(10, a), (20, b)\}$
III. $\{(a, 20)\}$
IV. $\{(10, b)\}$
explanation: A binary relation from $A$ to $B$ must be a subset of the Cartesian product $A \times B = \{(a, 10), (a, 20), (b, 10), (b, 20)\}$. Both I and III are subsets of $A \times B$, whereas II and IV are relations from $B$ to $A$. Thus I and III are valid.

explanation: By the Midpoint Theorem, the segment joining midpoints of two sides of a triangle is half of the third side: $DE = \frac{1}{2}AB \implies 16 = \frac{1}{2}(4x) \implies 16 = 2x \implies x = 8\text{ cm}$.
answer_origin: Official key cross-checked; explanations are supplementary

questionText: In the following figure, $BD$ is the angle bisector of $\angle ABC$. If $AB = 2\text{ cm}$, $BC = 6\text{ cm}$, and $CD = 3\text{ cm}$, then the length of $AD$ is
explanation: By the Angle Bisector Theorem: $\frac{AD}{CD} = \frac{AB}{BC} \implies \frac{AD}{3} = \frac{2}{6} = \frac{1}{3} \implies AD = 1\text{ cm}$.
